subject: POC environment: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Claire Liu <claire@novamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novamed.com
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: POC environment: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at NovaMed is keen to move this into a two-week evaluation that mirrors production traffic. To get the MAP and environment standing up quickly, we need:

- A clear checklist for org setup and roles (who creates the Redwood org, which service account to use).
- The API key provisioning flow (we prefer ephemeral keys if supported).
- IP allowlist ranges your runtime will use so our firewall team can open ports.
- VPC peering instructions and the expected CIDR ranges for route configuration.

Can you send a mutual action plan with these items and a target close timeline? We can have our infra lead (ops@novamed.com) and procurement on the thread.

Claire
Claire Liu
Director, Cloud Operations | NovaMed

[Attachment: initial_requirements.txt (text/plain)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Claire Liu <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: POC environment: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Hi Claire — really appreciate the quick follow-up. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP_NovaMed_v1.xlsx) that breaks the work into three streams: Org & Access, Network & Security, and Acceptance & Close. High level next steps I propose:

1) Org & Access (Day 0–2)
   - NovaMed confirms the primary Redwood org owner (we can also provision temporarily from our side).
   - Complete our API key request form (link in the MAP) — we will create either a scoped long-lived key or an ephemeral key depending on your preference.

2) Network & Security (Day 1–7)
   - Provide the IP ranges for outbound egress; we'll confirm the edges that need allowlisting.
   - VPC peering: provide your account/project id and desired CIDR; we will initiate a peering request and provide a template for your cloud team.

3) Acceptance & Close (Day 7–14)
   - Run a small load pass and a set of quality prompts we agree on.
   - Sign-off from NovaMed ops + procurement to move to a pilot.

Technical specifics / notes: we recommend ephemeral API keys with a 24h TTL for the evaluation, and we support both CIDR-based peering and IP allowlist depending on how locked down you want the environment. I attached the MAP and a template for the peering manifest.

Next steps for us: I'll loop Neha on technical details and Jordan for the contract cadence (if procurement wants a simple SOW or a Docusign path). Please review the MAP and add dates you prefer; if you can confirm your cloud account id and the contact for routing we can submit the peering request by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_NovaMed_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: peering_manifest_template.json (application/json)]

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Liu <claire@novamed.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-02T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: POC environment: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Thanks Claire / Irene — quick technical clarification from our infra side: 

- For VPC peering we prefer a non-overlapping /16 or /20 depending on NovaMed's existing ranges. If you can share the VPC CIDR you plan to peer, we'll draft the exact route and a Cloud Console step-by-step.
- Outbound IPs: our hosted runtime will originate from a small set of egress IP ranges per region; I'll include the precise CIDR block list in the peering request.
- Ephemeral API key behavior: recommendation is 24h TTL with an automated refresh endpoint. If you need a long-lived key for CI, we can scope it to read-only inference and rotate it halfway through the trial.

Irene — when I submit the peering request I will attach: the peering_manifest_template.json (filled), a sample firewall rule, and a test harness token for connectivity checks.

On the MAP: please confirm whether you want the peering to be initiated by us (Redwood) or by NovaMed — both are fine, but initiating from our side speeds the handshake for the trial.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
